subject: history_social
passage: Newgrange, a great mound of earth and stone in the valley of the River Boyne in Ireland, was built around 3200 BCE by farming communities that left no written record. A narrow passage leads to a central chamber under a corbeled stone roof that has kept the interior dry for five thousand years. Above the entrance sits a small opening, the roof-box, whose purpose was confirmed only in 1967, when the archaeologist Michael O'Kelly stood in the chamber at dawn on the winter solstice and watched sunlight travel up the passage. The ______ precision in aligning the opening with the midwinter sunrise has changed assumptions about the societies of Neolithic Europe.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The precision belonged to the people who built Newgrange, the "farming communities" of the first sentence, so the blank needs a plural possessive. A plural noun ending in s shows possession with an apostrophe alone: "builders'."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Builder's" is the possessive of a single builder, but the text says the mound was built by whole communities.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Builders" is a plain plural with no apostrophe, so it cannot show whose precision is meant.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A plural noun ending in s takes only an apostrophe to show possession; "builders's" is not standard.
explanation.D: Correct. "Builders'" is the plural possessive, showing that the precision was that of the many people who built the mound.
